original_question: For the Turan problem in the n-dimensional hypercube, let ex_k(n, d) denote the maximum number of k-dimensional subcubes in Q_n that avoid containing every k-subcube of any d-dimensional subcube, and let pi_k(d)=lim_{n->infinity} ex_k(n,d)/|Q_n^k| be the corresponding Turan density. Determine whether pi_k(3)=3/4 for each k in {0,1,2}.
target_in_paper: Section 1, Question 1.2 in “Turán problems in the hypercube”: the paper’s official small-case question asking whether π_k(3)=3/4 for k=0,1,2, presented immediately after Conjecture 1.1 and the surrounding definitions. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.18163))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right object, the right asymptotic parameter, and the right target value: it uses the paper’s extremal quantity ex_k(n,d), the density π_k(d), the ambient hypercube Q_n, and the exact small case k∈{0,1,2}, d=3 from Question 1.2. It also correctly paraphrases the avoidance condition as forbidding a family of k-subcubes from containing all k-subcubes of any 3-subcube. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.18163))
missing_details: The paper first defines a k-subcube of Q_n explicitly and denotes the set of all k-subcubes by Q_n^k; your draft uses this notation but does not define it stand-alone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.18163))

The containment relation between a d-subcube and a k-subcube is part of the setup, via the flip-bit/non-flip-bit description; this is implicit in your draft and should be stated explicitly if the question is to stand on its own. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.18163))

The paper’s official term is that a family S⊆Q_n^k is d-free if every d-subcube contains some k-subcube not in S; your draft paraphrases this but does not name or define the d-free condition in the paper’s language. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.18163))

The limit defining π_k(d) is part of the formal setup, and the paper notes that standard averaging arguments imply this limit exists; for a fully self-contained question, n should be understood to tend to infinity through the integers. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.18163))

The nearby broader context is Conjecture 1.1, of which Question 1.2 is the d=3 specialization; making that relationship explicit helps keep the question paper-faithful without broadening it. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.18163))

There are no ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions in this problem; the only missing ingredients are the combinatorial definitions and quantifiers above. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.18163))
refined_question: For each fixed k∈{0,1,2}, let Q_n^k denote the set of k-dimensional subcubes of the n-dimensional hypercube Q_n, and let ex_k(n,3) be the maximum size of a family S⊆Q_n^k that is 3-free, meaning that every 3-dimensional subcube of Q_n contains at least one k-subcube that does not belong to S. Define π_k(3):=lim_{n→∞} ex_k(n,3)/|Q_n^k|. Is it true that π_k(3)=3/4 for each k∈{0,1,2}? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.18163))
justification: The draft is already very close, but the nearest official formulation in the paper is not a broad conjectural restatement: it is exactly Question 1.2 in Section 1. The preceding paragraph in Section 1 supplies the notation Q_n^k, the containment relation for subcubes, the definition of d-free families, the extremal function ex_k(n,d), and the density π_k(d); Conjecture 1.1 supplies the immediate context, and Question 1.2 then isolates the concrete d=3 case for k=0,1,2. So the sharp paper-faithful refinement is simply to make those surrounding definitions explicit and ask the question in the paper’s own d-free language. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2310.18163))
